_readme: Owner gates for the autonomous dispatch loop, enforced by .claude/hooks/plan-guard.mjs.
These are the actions an agent must never take unattended, however good its reasons.
Prompts degrade over a long run; this file does not — it is the actual boundary.
The defaults below are project-agnostic: hard-to-reverse, outward-facing, or
credential-bearing. ADD YOUR PROJECT'S OWN, especially: production feature-flag
flips, anything that reaches a live customer, and any command that costs money.
Keep this file and the owner-gate section of your work plan in sync — a gate that
exists in prose but not here is not a gate. Add a case to plan-guard.test.mjs with
every new entry, and run: node .claude/hooks/plan-guard.test.mjs
Fields: pattern = JS regex source (case-insensitive) tested against the Bash
command; scanContent = also reject file writes whose CONTENT matches.

commandGates.why: Force-push discards history that may not exist anywhere else.
History rewriting is unrecoverable for anyone who already pulled.
Deleting a remote branch destroys work the agent cannot restore.
Deploying is outward-facing and often auto-applies migrations the agent cannot undo.
Infrastructure mutation is expensive and hard to reverse.
Reaching a live host steps outside the repo, where nothing is reviewable or revertible.
Publishing is public and effectively permanent.
Pulls live credentials into a transcript.
Enabling a production feature flag is an owner decision. REPLACE this pattern with your project's real flag names.

pathGates.why: Deploy, infrastructure and CI definitions run against real environments.
